scores.rationale: The detached clean HEAD matches the named candidate; contract and candidate fingerprints reproduced independently from the commit tree. The version-four baseline, A-N donor decisions, selective-integration policy, changed-path coverage, and no-merge history are pinned and complete.

Canonical records remain authoritative, the ten-page exact set carries valid canonical references, and lifecycle checks cover graph closure, intake disposition, proof debt, citations, duplicates, unknown references, and retired wording. Candidate-specific dependency-free inspection found all required stable IDs and authority-bearing structures.

Agency relations classify the proof layer as an exact set with bounded action, usable result, credit scope, confidence, canonical support or explicit debt, and anti-claims. Mutations explicitly reject missing classifications, solo causality, title inflation, collaborator erasure, and endorsement drift; the new pages consistently preserve collective credit.

The operator interfaces are thin wrappers over canonical records: intake is validate-only or exclusive-create and never promotes claims, query is read-only and bounded, and the leak scanner fails closed. Source tests cover unsafe input, unknown references, broken graphs, invalid views, private locators, credentials, and absent compiled output. Full command execution was unavailable because this clean sandbox lacks installed dependencies and Node 26.

Survivorship uses an exact status vocabulary and bounded negative-search language; six rights dimensions remain separate, protected scans stay outside Git, and discoveries cannot promote automatically. The source-return receipt distinguishes public, protected aggregate-only, and metadata-only sources and routes new evidence back through source, claim, inquiry, correction, and projection review.

The composition manifest accounts for every public route or template with audience, argument, action, budget, selections, and omissions. Exact-set and budget mutations cover proof and direct-projection drift, while the candidate-bound mosaic review records eight cross-fragment risks and continuing omission or generalization holds.

This receipt independently reproduced the frozen contract and exact candidate fingerprints, verified its own read-only binding, and found all 23 candidate-changed paths inside the 104-path fingerprint scope. Receipt schemas, candidate drift, self-grading, duplicate scores, invented evidence, and aggregate derivation are mutation-tested. Score 4 is correctly withheld for the later two-receipt aggregate.

Source-layer release policy is coherent: the full check sequence includes graph, source-return, composite, leak, public-safety, and route gates; staging and production indexing policies are separate; browser, accessibility, runtime, and human QA remain distinct evidence layers. Exact runtime and browser layers were not rerun because the sandbox has Node 24 and no installed dependencies.

PR-019 and PR-025 remain pending human review with explicit blockers and no reviewer or candidate falsely attached. Librarian, collaborator, rights, consent, editorial, production, and indexing decisions remain open; tests reject automated approval and preserve exact-candidate human release authority.
